stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, and its shares jump 33% at the open
stories.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO on Monday, days after rejecting his offer to return; its shares opened 33% higher at $165.57, the AP reports. President Trump said his intervention was 'very important'.

predictions.note: Trump said his intervention was 'very important' in the board's decision to bring back the CEO of the leading AI chipmaker.

stories.title: Meta's AI chief Alexandr Wang: 'Superintelligence is arriving'
stories.summary: After a mathematician said he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang posted on X that 'superintelligence is arriving' and that how humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence, Al Jazeera reports.

stories.title: Z.ai's GLM-5.4 runs its layers twice to rival much bigger models
stories.summary: Z.ai released GLM-5.4, a 750-billion-parameter 'looped' model that runs 28 layers of its GLM-5 base twice. The company says it matches models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters, but it published no benchmark scores.

stories.title: Claude use by Japanese companies is up tenfold in a year
stories.summary: Use of Anthropic's Claude by Japanese companies and organisations has increased tenfold over the past year, Nikkei Asia reports.

stories.title: Amazon buys Decart's chip-optimisation tech and team, reportedly for $7.5 billion
stories.summary: Amazon is acquiring the technology behind Decart's optimisation stack, which helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon and Google chips, plus its founders and researchers, for $7.5 billion according to Bloomberg, as it prepares to sell its Trainium chips to customers.

stories.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal
stories.summary: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record according to Reuters; the companies say it will help customers adopt AI safely.

stories.title: Ant Group leads a $100 million round in humanoid robot maker Simplexity
stories.summary: Chinese physical AI startup Simplexity Robotics received $100 million in a funding round led by Jack Ma-backed Ant Group, Bloomberg reports.

stories.title: NHS invites nearly 700,000 women to the world's largest AI breast-screening trial
stories.summary: Nearly 700,000 women across the UK will be invited to the EDITH trial, in which AI replaces one of the two human readers of each mammogram, the BBC reports; recruitment has begun at Cambridge, the first of 30 sites.

stories.title: Paradromics teams up with Nvidia to shrink its brain-implant speech decoder
stories.summary: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics will use Nvidia hardware and software to turn the cart of electronics that decodes a Michigan woman's speech implant into a small box on her wheelchair within a year, Wired reports.

predictions.note: A speech-decoding brain implant is set to move from a cart of electronics to a box on the user's wheelchair, using Nvidia hardware.

stories.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX and X over Grok's sexual deepfakes
stories.summary: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia sued SpaceX and X Corp., alleging they broke consumer protection laws by misleading users about Grok's safety and about stopping child sexual abuse material and nonconsensual intimate images.

stories.title: Over 150 child safety groups urge Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys
stories.summary: More than 150 child safety groups and experts across six continents asked Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys this Christmas until they are proved safe, and to offer refunds, the Guardian reports.

stories.title: Unitree shares jump the 20% daily limit as China backs care robots
stories.summary: Unitree Robotics shares rose by the 20% daily limit on Monday to close at 708 yuan, as four Chinese government departments released a plan encouraging service robots and exoskeletons for elderly care, the Global Times reports.

stories.title: Türkiye opens grants covering half the cost of industrial humanoid robot projects
stories.summary: Türkiye opened applications on 23 November for humanoid-robot development projects for industrial use, with grants covering 50% of project budgets, Industry and Technology Minister Mehmet Fatih Kacır announced.

stories.title: Novartis CEO rejects hopes that AI will cure cancer within five to 10 years
stories.summary: Novartis chief executive Vas Narasimhan, who sits on Anthropic's board, rejected the idea that AI will cure cancer within five to 10 years, the Financial Times reports.

predictions.note: Novartis's CEO, an Anthropic board member, rejects the idea that AI will cure cancer within five to 10 years.

stories.title: Some US banks tighten controls on their own AI agents, Reuters reports
stories.summary: Several large and mid-sized US banks are tightening controls around their own AI agents to stop them going rogue, over concern that models could escape safeguards, according to a Reuters exclusive.

predictions.note: Banks are voluntarily tightening controls on their own AI agents over concern that the models could escape safeguards.

transcript.t: It's Tuesday, November 24, and this is the Singularity Daily.
Here's your day in superintelligence, in 3 minutes flat.
What a comeback. Days after saying no, Nvidia just gave Jensen Huang his job back.
The stock jumped 33% at the opening bell.
Meanwhile, Meta's AI chief, Alexandr Wang, put it in three words: superintelligence is arriving.
He says what we do over the next year will shape the world we live in.
In China, Z.ai says its new model runs its layers twice, to match models 3 times bigger.
And in Japan, companies are using Anthropic's Claude 10 times as much as a year ago.
Now, the money. Amazon's buying Decart's chip-tuning tech, reportedly for $7.5 billion.
Why? Amazon's getting ready to sell its own AI chips, right up against Nvidia.
And CrowdStrike is buying Zscaler for $44 billion, the biggest cybersecurity deal on record.
Plus, Ant Group led a $100 million bet on Simplexity, a Chinese humanoid robot startup.
Over in Britain, nearly 700,000 women are being invited into the biggest AI breast-screening trial yet.
Mary talks through a brain implant, and Nvidia's chips will shrink its computer cart to a small box.
The catch? Oregon and Virginia are suing SpaceX over Grok's sexual deepfakes.
And over 150 child-safety groups want AI toys pulled from sale.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
In China, robot maker Unitree's shares jumped 20%, the most allowed in a day.
The same day, Beijing unveiled a plan to bring care robots and exoskeletons into nursing homes.
And Türkiye will now cover half the cost of p rojects building humanoid robots for industry.
Nothing's final. Not a firing, not a sell-off, and not our say in what comes next.
Zoom out, and the line only goes up.
And the future keeps arriving ahead of schedule.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
You've been watching the Singularity Daily.
See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
